# Results — Study 874 (IPO-Price Anchoring)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — investors
**anchor** on an IPO's **offer price**, so (1) the forward return should be *negatively* related
to the current gap-from-offer (a slow pull back toward the anchor) and (2) trading *below* the
offer should be a persistent drag. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar
month; the partial current month is dropped). Stamped as-of 2026-06-30. Fingerprint `1eaa178051af`
(monthly close panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Curated table | **44 well-known recent US listings** (40 underwritten IPOs + 4 direct listings) with their public **offer / reference price** and **first-trade date**, hard-coded in `data.py` from the public record (SEC EDGAR 424B4 prospectuses; exchange reference-price notices) |
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return) for every curated ticker plus **`SPY`** (market leg), cached under this study's own `_cache/`, 2014-01 → 2026-06 |
| Panel | name-month observations from each name's first full trading month; **86 active months** (≥ 5 live names), **2,698 name-months**, avg **30.3** names/active month, below-offer share **42.0%** |
| Anchor | `gap = log(price / offer)` measured at each month-end (the behavioural distance from the round offer number); `below` flag = price < offer |
| Forward return | each name's **next-month total return minus `SPY`'s** (market-adjusted), so generic IPO-cohort underperformance (study 623) is netted out |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: gap/flag through close of month `t` → predict month `t+1`. The costed timer charges 2 × one-way × NAV per leg on the monthly re-hedge; the short (below-offer) leg pays borrow |
| Statistics | monthly **Fama-MacBeth** cross-sectional slope with a Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t*; a below-offer − above-offer basket spread with a HAC *t*; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship / curation — named on the Signal axis.** The 44 names are *chosen from memory*
of famous recent IPOs — a curation skewed toward the splashy 2020-21 cohort that rose and
crashed together. We deliberately KEEP later-delisted names (e.g. an acquired issuer), the
opposite of survivorship pruning, but the *selection* bias remains: this is a small, one-cohort
sample, so any magnitude below is an anecdote-grade estimate and the *t*'s are the honest arbiter.

## Test 1 — the anchoring pull (Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional slope)

Each month, regress the forward market-adjusted return on the gap-from-offer across the live
names; average the monthly slopes; HAC *t* over months. **Anchoring predicts a negative slope.**

| sample | mean slope | bps/mo per +10% above offer | NW(6) *t* | months neg. | n months |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **all 44 listings** | **−0.0023** | **−2.3** | **−0.39** | 44% | 86 |
| IPOs only (40) | −0.0018 | −1.8 | −0.30 | 45% | 85 |

The slope is **the right sign** (negative — stretched-above names do lag) but **nowhere near
significant** (NW *t* = −0.39). The gap-from-offer carries essentially no forward information.

## Test 2 — the below-offer drag (below-offer minus above-offer basket)

Each month, mean forward market-adjusted return of the below-offer names minus that of the
above-offer names. **The drag claim predicts a negative spread.**

| sample | spread (bps/mo) | ann. | NW(6) *t* | Welch *t* | n months |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **all 44 listings** | **−56.84** | −6.61%/yr | **−0.56** | −0.35 | 76 |
| IPOs only (40) | −99.93 | −11.35%/yr | −0.94 | −0.61 | 74 |

Below-offer names *did* trail above-offer names by a chunky-looking **−57 bps/mo**
(below basket +13.1 vs above basket +69.9 bps/mo, market-adjusted) — but with **NW *t* = −0.56**
it is indistinguishable from noise. This is exactly the trap the desk exists to flag: an
economically loud number with a *t* that says "sample of one cohort".

## Placebo — is the (tiny) slope a lucky alignment of gap and forward return?

Shuffle the gap → forward-return pairing *within each month* (each month's own distributions
preserved), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | **−0.00233** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.00026 (0.00478) |
| left-tail *p* | **0.322** |
| two-sided *p* | **0.610** |

The observed slope sits comfortably *inside* the permutation null — it cannot be told apart from
a random pairing. No anchoring pull to speak of.

## Robustness — the below-offer spread across two eras (split 2022-07)

| era | spread (bps/mo) | NW(6) *t* | n months |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-2022-07 | −43.31 | −0.18 | 29 |
| 2022-07 on | −65.19 | −0.87 | 47 |

The drag keeps the **same (negative) sign** in both halves — consistent, but insignificant in
each. Consistency of an *insignificant* sign is not evidence; it is what a single correlated
cohort looks like sliced two ways.

## The timer — can you get paid for the (insignificant) drag?

Trade the drag as SHORT below-offer / LONG above-offer; monthly re-hedge pays 2 × one-way × NAV
per leg; the short (below-offer, small-cap recent-IPO) leg pays borrow.

| one-way cost | borrow | gross/mo | gross *t* | net/mo | net *t* | ann. | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **10 bps** | 3%/yr | +56.84 bps | +0.56 | **+11.84 bps** | +0.12 | +1.43%/yr | −57.0% |
| **20 bps** | 5%/yr | +56.84 bps | +0.56 | **−24.82 bps** | −0.24 | −2.94%/yr | −61.7% |

Even the *gross* long-short earns only +56.8 bps/mo at *t* = +0.56 (a coin-flip); realistic
recent-IPO borrow plus costs push net to a rounding error (+11.8 bps) or negative (−24.8 bps),
riding a ~60% drawdown. No paycheck.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded name-month panel with a persistent gap that (with `edge > 0`) pulls the
forward return back toward the offer anchor. No network. 20 seeds per row.

| world | mean FM slope | mean HAC *t* | \|t\| ≥ 2 rejection rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`) | +0.0023 | +0.41 | **0%** |
| planted (`edge = 0.15`) | −0.1441 | −12.54 | **100%** |
| planted (`edge = 0.30`) | −0.2946 | −19.76 | **100%** |

The detector recovers a *planted* anchoring pull cleanly and never fires on the null — so the
flat real-tape result is a genuine absence of the effect (or a sample too small to see it), not
a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited for the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Neither leg of the anchoring story survives. The Fama-MacBeth
  anchoring-pull slope is **−0.0023** (NW *t* = **−0.39**; placebo two-sided *p* = 0.61); the
  below-offer drag is a loud-looking **−56.8 bps/mo** but **NW *t* = −0.56**, same sign in both
  sub-eras yet insignificant in each. Both point the way the claim predicts and neither clears
  |t| ≥ 2 — a textbook underpowered, one-cohort curated cross-section. The clean 20-seed
  synthetic control (fires on 0/20 nulls, 100% on a planted pull) proves the flatness is real,
  not machinery. *Curation bias named on the Signal axis.*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The tradable short-below / long-above book earns +56.8 bps/mo
  *gross* at *t* = +0.56; borrow + costs take it to +11.8 → −24.8 bps/mo (*t* ≈ +0.12 → −0.24)
  on a ~60% drawdown. There is no edge to harvest.
